blockers.fix: Copy the exact callback URL from the app settings into your authorize request, including host and port, and check path prefix rules.

blockers.blocker: Token has fewer scopes than expected
blockers.fix: Users can edit scopes on consent. Check the token scopes returned and handle a reduced scope gracefully.

blockers.blocker: Confusing GitHub App vs OAuth app
blockers.fix: GitHub Apps use fine-grained permissions, not scopes in the authorize request. Pick OAuth app only if you specifically need the OAuth app model.

steps.blockerTip: The callback URL must match exactly, including host, port, and path prefix rules. A mismatch is the most common first failure.
steps.detail: In Developer settings, choose OAuth Apps, then New OAuth App. Add an application name, homepage URL, and authorization callback URL.
steps.title: Create the OAuth app

steps.blockerTip: Treat a leaked secret as compromised. Regenerate it and rotate any tokens made with it.
steps.detail: Copy the client ID and generate a client secret. Store the secret securely, never in client code or in a public repo.
steps.title: Save the client ID and client secret

steps.blockerTip: Asking for repo when you only need public data will scare users and reviewers, even if no formal approval is required.
steps.detail: Request only the scopes your agent actually uses, for example read:user for profile data or repo only if private repo access is truly needed. Scopes limit access, they do not grant more than the user already has.
steps.title: Choose the minimum scopes

steps.blockerTip: Always check the state value on return. Skipping it leaves the flow open to forgery.
steps.detail: Redirect the user to github.com/login/oauth/authorize with client_id, redirect_uri, scope, and a random state value. Exchange the returned code for an access token, then call the API with that token.
steps.title: Build the authorization flow

steps.blockerTip: If the consent screen shows extra scopes, fix the authorize URL, not the app settings alone.
steps.detail: Authorize the app with a test account, confirm the consent screen shows only the scopes you requested, and confirm a token works for one real API call.
steps.title: Test with your own account
